question.text: The derivatives trading platform used by NSE is called:

answer.text: NEAT-F&O (National Exchange for Automated Trading - Futures & Options)

explanation.text: The Logic: NSE's cash-market platform is historically referred to as NEAT (National Exchange for Automated Trading), and the derivatives extension of that platform has been branded NEAT-F&O. It is the fully automated, screen-based, anonymous, order-driven matching system that members access from their trading terminals to enter futures and options orders. The Trap: BOLT (BSE On-Line Trading) is BSE's trading system, not NSE's. ODIN is a third-party trading front-end software used by brokers, not an exchange platform. CTCL (Computer-To-Computer Link) is a connectivity facility that lets a broker's own system communicate with the exchange — it is not itself the exchange trading platform. Note: The cited NISM Series VIII Equity Derivatives workbook describes Indian F&O trading as electronic, fully automated and screen-based, but the pages checked do not name the platform as "NEAT-F&O" / "National Exchange for Automated Trading". The naming above is general industry knowledge about NSE's exchange infrastructure.
